baseline_of_record.name: concordance_modern_final_v2.json
baseline_of_record.note: The first two run receipts referenced concordance32_CORRECTED.json (sha256 e92d79fe8c77e0f8b1a073ffc67524ae83bc2532796d9d2f1fc72753bebf24b3); its 0.5B and 1.5B values are identical to the modern-final receipt in all twelve sessions. The other five receipts directly reference modern-final.

protocol.alpha_selection: RidgeCV GCV on each outer training fold only
protocol.expanded_grid: union of original grid and numpy.logspace(7, 14, 8)
protocol.score: mean over 30 neural target columns of held-out Pearson correlation with original +1e-12 denominator epsilon

size_ordering_descriptive.interpretation: The finite original alpha grid materially steepened the measured decline, particularly at 32B. The 72B score remains below 0.5B under the expanded original scorer. Seven-rung rank significance is not retained, but n=7 is small and this does not prove a flat scaling law.

seventy_two_b_limit_diagnostic.three_distinct_estimands: 0.0449093227 is train-selected 11x1e14 plus fold9 interior alpha under the original epsilon scorer. 0.0450516792 uses the same train-selected alphas but removes epsilon attenuation at the 11 high-alpha folds. 0.0458094248 uses fixed alpha 1e14 in all twelve folds and scale-free Pearson; it is a different policy because fold9 changes alpha.
seventy_two_b_limit_diagnostic.interpretation: Prediction direction reaches a large-penalty limit by 1e12; no interior finite-alpha optimum is established. At the same fixed 1e14 policy, original fixed-epsilon scoring attenuates the mean by 0.000142864. Do not attribute the larger 0.000900102 difference between fixed-limit scale-free and train-selected original scores solely to epsilon: fold 9 uses an interior alpha under the train-selected policy.

provenance_correction.reason: Generator SHA was initially read from the on-disk script at job end. The same remote file received a later plateau-only extension while 14B and 72B were already running; their saved generator_sha256 fields therefore reflect the newer on-disk version, though the in-memory fit/scoring code came from the earlier committed version.
provenance_correction.fit_and_scoring_difference: none; the later extension added a separate plateau mode and start-time hashing, without changing the primary RidgeCV branch
